bd-2390 made the module quiz a gate, so the two halves of the loop call each other: content-delivery.handleModuleDone lazy-requires quiz-delivery to send the quiz, and quiz-delivery.gradeAttempt lazy-requires content-delivery.deliverNextModule to release the next module once the teacher passes. BOTH requires are inside function bodies, never at module top level, so neither ever observes a half-initialised `{}`. The two halves of one send. transcript-quiz-generate finishes authoring and lazy-requires transcript-quiz-handoff to mint the share code, attach the PDF and pace the three messages — the same routine /quiz "resend the link" runs on a quiz that already went out, which is why it lives on the hand-off side. The hand-off in turn lazy-requires generate for studentMessage(), renderPdf(), withFigureSvgs() and pdfFilename() when it has to rebuild a PDF that is no longer on R2. EVERY require on both sides is inside a function body, never at module top level, so neither module can observe the other half-initialised as `{}` — which is the failure this guard exists to catch. Splitting the four shared renderers into a fourth module is the real fix and is filed; it is a refactor of the authoring path, not something to do inside a cherry-pick onto production.
